name: One category orders drop 40%
description: Category 'Electronics' orders drop 40% for a week while other categories remain steady.

name: One state spikes
description: Orders in state 'California' spike by 150% due to regional marketing campaign.

name: Discount day raises units and lowers AOV
description: Site-wide promotional discount reduces prices across categories, lowering AOV driven by rate effect.

name: Tracking break sends one source to zero
description: Analytics tracking outage sends 'Google Organic' traffic and orders to zero in current period.

name: Mix shift to cheaper category lowers AOV
description: Customers purchase higher volume of cheap 'Accessories' and fewer expensive 'Electronics', lowering AOV via mix effect with no price changes.

name: Prices fall inside every category
description: Universal markdown reduces sale prices inside every category with constant customer category mix.

name: Two overlapping causes: one large, one small
description: Primary drop in category 'Apparel' (-$3000) coupled with secondary drop in 'Home' (-$600).

name: Weekday dip control (routine cycle)
description: Normal cyclical weekday decline from Sunday to Tuesday. Should not be crowned as an anomaly cause.

name: Incomplete current day
description: Current date only has 5 hours of partial data ingested compared to full 24-hour baseline day.

name: Noise control (no planted change)
description: Normal statistical noise in steady state. Engine should say within normal volatility and report Low confidence.

name: Low support segment spike
description: Segment 'Specialty Rare' with only 4 orders spikes by 200%. Should be marked low support and not high confidence.

name: Offsetting gains and losses that cancel
description: Large revenue increase in 'Electronics' (+2500) cancels with large drop in 'Apparel' (-2450), net change is only +50.

name: N1 Small effect: one category falls 10 percent
description: Category 'Electronics' falls 10% in current week. Expected: if a driver is named it is that category; confidence is not High unless change is outside normal range.

name: N2 Two-way segment: state=California AND source=Paid Search
description: Orders fall only where state = California AND traffic source = Paid Search; other California and other Search orders unaffected. Expected: top finding is the two-way segment, not CA or Search alone.

name: N3 Mix versus rate: AOV rises while category prices fall
description: Overall AOV rises, while AOV inside every category falls slightly (-5%), because customers shift heavily to a pricier category. Expected: mix effect positive and dominant, rate effects negative; evidence must not suggest prices rose.

name: N4 Duplicate load: all rows for one day loaded twice
description: All rows for one day are loaded twice due to pipeline replay. Expected: duplicate-jump flag, Low or Medium confidence, no business driver.

name: N5 Null spike: state becomes NULL for 30 percent of rows
description: State becomes NULL for 30 percent of rows from start of current window. Expected: null-spike flag; NULL is not presented as a business driver; no real state is blamed.

name: N6 Broad decline: revenue falls 8 percent evenly
description: Revenue falls 8 percent evenly across all categories, states and sources. Expected: no single driver, Low confidence, evidence says the decline is broad-based.

name: N7 New segment: category with 0 baseline orders appears
description: A category with no baseline orders ('New Innovation') appears with 120 orders in current window. Expected: named as a new-segment driver of the increase, with a note that it appears from zero.
